summary: This document defines IPFIX Information Elements for exporting information about Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6). That includes data in the Segment Routing Header, the SRv6 control plane, and the SRv6 endpoint behavior used to forward traffic. This lets flow collectors see SRv6 traffic.

plainLanguage.summary: A traffic counter at the road logs each car. This adds new boxes to the logbook for the special routes that SRv6 cars follow.

questions: what is the segment routing header
subtitle: Eleven new IPFIX fields that let flow exporters report what Segment Routing over IPv6 traffic is doing.

tldr.problem: Flow monitoring with IPFIX had no standard fields for Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6), so data in the Segment Routing Header, the control plane that supplied a segment, and the endpoint behavior could not be exported.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9487 defines eleven new IPFIX Information Elements (IDs 492 to 502) and one new subregistry, covering the SRH flags, tag, segment list, active segment, segments left, the active segment's source protocol, locator length and endpoint behavior.
tldr.outcome: Collectors can answer questions such as which segment list a flow used, what the active segment is and how many segments are left. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 9487 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2023, and it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why SRv6 Needs New IPFIX Fields
sections.content:
In Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6), a dedicated routing extension header called the Segment Routing Header (SRH, RFC 8754) carries a list of segments for a packet to follow. Segment Identifiers (SIDs) are spread by routing protocols and by PCEP: OSPFv3, IS-IS (RFC 9352) and BGP Prefix-SIDs (RFC 8669), plus the Segment Routing Policy (RFC 9256). How a node processes a segment is called an endpoint behavior, defined in RFC 8986.

RFC 9487 specifies eleven new IPFIX Information Elements (IEs) and one new subregistry in the IPFIX Information Elements registry (RFC 7012). They export the active SRv6 segment and its control plane protocol, the Segment List, the next SRv6 node and its type, and the number of segments left.
sections.plainLanguage: Flow records are like a logbook of traffic. SRv6 traffic follows a list of stops, and the logbook had no boxes for writing that list down. This RFC adds the boxes.

sections.title: The New Information Elements
sections.content:
The IEs are numbered 492 to 502. Several simply copy an SRH field: srhFlagsIPv6 (492) is the 8-bit Flags field and srhTagIPv6 (493) is the 16-bit Tag, which marks a packet as part of a class or group sharing properties. srhSegmentsIPv6Left (498) is the number of segments remaining to the end of the Segment List.

Others carry addresses: srhSegmentIPv6 (494) is a 128-bit IPv6 address for one SRv6 segment and srhActiveSegmentIPv6 (495) is the active segment. The Segment List itself can be exported as a srhSegmentIPv6BasicList (496), an ordered basicList of zero or more addresses, or as a raw srhSegmentIPv6ListSection (497). The whole SRH with its TLVs can be exported as srhIPv6Section (499).

The last three describe context. srhIPv6ActiveSegmentType (500) says which routing protocol or PCEP extension the active segment was learned from. srhSegmentIPv6LocatorLength (501) gives the locator length in significant bits and, with srhSegmentIPv6, lets you compute the SRv6 Locator. srhSegmentIPv6EndpointBehavior (502) is a 16-bit endpoint behavior value from RFC 8986. The IEs 494, 501 and 502 are generic and intended for Options Templates or structured data.
sections.plainLanguage: Each new box in the logbook holds one fact about the route: the stops on the map, the stop you are at, how many stops remain, and how the stop was learned.

sections.title: Exporting the Segment List
sections.content:
The Segment List can be exported two ways, and the RFC does not expect an exporter to support both. The basicList form (RFC 6313) arrives already structured, so the collector needs no post-processing, but the exporter must do extra work to build it.

The octet array form imposes no data flow manipulation on the exporter, so export is immediate and the records are slightly shorter. The cost moves to the collector, which MUST be able to decode the IPv6 addresses according to the SR specifications. The Segment List is encoded starting from the last segment of the SR Policy, so Segment List[0] holds the last segment.

The Segment List in these IEs, and in destinationIPv6Address, could hold compressed-SID containers as described in a draft on compressed SRv6 segment lists. A collector can decode them using the endpoint behavior and locator length IEs.
sections.plainLanguage: You can write the list of stops as a neat table or as one long string of letters. The table is easier to read but harder to write, and the string is the other way round.

sections.title: Use Cases and Encoding Examples
sections.content:
Together with forwardingStatus (89) and existing counters, the IEs 496 or 497, 495, 498 and 500 help answer questions like: how many packets steered with an SR policy are forwarded or dropped using SRv6, and why dropped; what the active segment and its control plane protocol are; what the Segment List is; what the next SRv6 node and its type are; and how many segments are left.

Appendix A shows full IPFIX encodings for three observed SRHs, each with Flags 0, Tags 123, 456 and 789, and active segment type IS-IS (value 4). It uses Template IDs 256 (basicList), 257 (list section) and 258 (whole SRH section). A second example uses Template ID 259, an Options Template where srhActiveSegmentIPv6 is the scope field, mapping segments to an endpoint behavior (End is 1, End with NEXT-CSID is 43, End.DX6 is 16) and a locator length of 48.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show, byte by byte, how three sample routes and their notes are packed into a message the collector can read back.

sections.title: The Segment Type Subregistry
sections.content:
IANA added the eleven IEs to the IPFIX Information Elements registry and created a subregistry called "IPFIX IPv6 SRH Segment Type (Value 500)". New entries need Expert Review (RFC 8126), and the designated experts should be familiar with the SRH and check that a request does not duplicate an existing entry and has a clear description.

The initial values are 0 Unknown, 1 Segment Routing Policy, 2 Path Computation Element, 3 OSPFv3 Segment Routing, 4 IS-IS Segment Routing and 5 BGP Segment Routing Prefix-SID.
sections.plainLanguage: A numbered list says where a stop on the route came from, such as a rulebook, a map office or a neighbour who told you.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC finds no additional security considerations for allocating these IEs beyond those of RFC 7012. It does note that the IEs export provider-plane data on how packets are forwarded in an SRv6 network.

Operators must judge how sensitive that information is in their setting and apply the data-at-rest storage guidance in Section 11.8 of RFC 7011 as appropriate.
sections.plainLanguage: The logbook shows how traffic moves through your network, so keep it somewhere safe.
